taxonomy.subtopic: Primary-cilium signaling and intracranial saccular aneurysm association

questions.stem_html:
A 43-year-old man with hypertension develops intermittent flank discomfort and gross hematuria after minor exercise. Imaging shows bilaterally enlarged kidneys containing numerous cysts and several hepatic cysts. His mother required dialysis at age 61, and his older sister survived rupture of an intracranial aneurysm.

Which additional lesion is this patient at increased risk of harboring?

options.text_html: A saccular aneurysm at a branch point in the circle of Willis
A fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm caused by tertiary syphilis
A capillary hemangioblastoma of the cerebellum

questions.explanation_html: PKD1 or PKD2 dysfunction alters primary-cilium-dependent tubular signaling and promotes cyst formation. ADPKD also predisposes to intracranial saccular aneurysms, especially with a family history of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. The family history and ADPKD phenotype specifically raise concern for a berry aneurysm in the circle of Willis.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Syphilitic aortitis affects the ascending thoracic aorta and is not the characteristic vascular association of ADPKD.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Hemangioblastomas are associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease rather than ADPKD.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Pulmonary AVMs are classically linked to hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Mycotic aneurysms arise from infection and are not a typical inherited extrarenal manifestation of ADPKD.

questions.educational_objective: Recognize the major extrarenal manifestations of ADPKD, including hepatic cysts and intracranial saccular aneurysms, and identify family history as an important risk signal.
